title: Perception Gaps in Precision Livestock Farming Adoption: Cross-National Evidence from Finland  and Albania
content: Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) technologies can improve the socio-economic and environmental performance of livestock farms. However, the differences between the benefits perceived by current adopters and the expectations of farmers planning to adopt them, and how this gap varies across national contexts, remain underexamined. The study examines the gap between the perceived benefits of farmers currently using PLF technologies and the expectations of planned adopters, comparing two countries with different levels of adoption maturity, Finland and Albania. Combining Expectation Confirmation Theory (ECT) with Diffusion of Innovations Theory (DoI), the study uses a structured survey of 73 cattle farms (32 current adopters and 41 planned adopters); differences were assessed using Mann-Whitney U tests, effect sizes, and confidence intervals. Perceptions of current adopters were comparable between the two countries, with no statistically significant differences in the socio-economic and environmental dimensions. Conversely, the expectations of planned adopters differed substantially, with a wider gap in the environmental dimension. The gap was large in Albania but minor in Finland, indicating that the magnitude and direction of the disconfirmation vary with PLF adoption maturity. These findings extend ECT beyond individual-level analysis and provide practical guidance for tailoring advisory services across different stages of PLF adoption.
